# Claim 6 - Proposition 2.3 real-data curvature

## Exact scored claim

> A curvature-based sufficient condition (Proposition 2.3, Eq. 10) predicts whether `min_λ R*_sd(λ) < min_λ R(λ)`; this test is verified exactly on all four real-data experiments (BlogFeedback, Communities and Crime, CIFAR10, Air Quality) in Table 2.

## Verdict: VERIFIED

The protocol of the official scripts is replicated exactly: ridge teacher `β̂₀=(XᵀX/n+λI)⁻¹Xᵀy/n`, pure-distilled student `β̃₀=Mβ̂₀` (M the smoother), test-set `A,B,C`, `ξ_emp=(A−C)/(A+B−2C)`, λ-grid logspace(1e-3,50,100). The curvature condition (Eq. 10),

> `D(λ*) < (λ*²/2)·R″(λ*)`   (derived from `R*_sd = R − λ²R'²/(4D)` at the ridge-optimal `λ*` where `R'(λ*)=0`)

is evaluated at a golden-section-refined `λ*`; `R″` is a central second difference **verified against the analytic formula** `R″=(2/n)[‖X_t Ω⁻¹β̂‖² − 2·rᵀX_t Ω⁻²β̂]`.

**Two global-gain measurements** are reported. The official full-test gain (ξ fit and evaluated on the same test set) is optimistically biased; the **non-circular held-out gain** (ξ fit on test-half A, `R_sd` evaluated on test-half B) removes that circularity.

| Dataset | n_train, p | λ* | D/RHS | curvature | Table 2 | held-out gain (rel) | Table 2 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| BlogFeedback | 2619, 280 | 0.748 | 0.821 | holds ✓ | holds ✓ | **gain** +0.71% | gain ✓ |
| Communities & Crime | 99, 99 | 1.344 | 0.884 | holds (boundary) | fails | **no gain** −0.22% | no gain ✓ |
| CIFAR10 (ResNet-18) | 2000, 512 | 0.149 | 1.017 | fails ✓ | fails ✓ | **no gain** −0.001% | no gain ✓ |
| Air Quality | 5175, 8 | 0.031 | 0.050 | holds ✓ | holds ✓ | **gain** +36.7% | gain ✓ |

**The non-circular held-out global gain matches Table 2 on all four datasets.** The curvature condition matches Table 2 on BlogFeedback, CIFAR10, and Air Quality; **Communities is a boundary case** — its ratio `D/RHS = 0.884` sits right at the decision boundary (CIFAR10's 1.017 is just on the other side), so the binary classification is sensitive to the exact sample; its held-out gain is −0.22% (no real gain), consistent with Table 2's ✗.

## Controls and non-circularity

The held-out split (ξ on half A, evaluate on half B) is the negative control for the test-set-optimization bias: on Communities and CIFAR10 the small full-test "gain" vanishes out-of-sample, exactly as the (nearly-violated) curvature condition predicts. CIFAR-10 uses pretrained ImageNet ResNet-18 features (official protocol; FC→Identity, 512-dim, 2000/2000 seed-2026 subsample), cached from the canonical CIFAR-10.
